name: Yoked rings, 100+10 ms CCW, partner sees light flashes (Persinger 2010)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Persinger, Saroka, Lavallee, Booth, Hunter, Mulligan, Koren, Wu & Gang 2010), yoked circumcerebral rings
summary: The shared field of Persinger et al. 2010: two unrelated people 5 to 10 m apart wear eight-coil rings driven together, on one counter-clockwise rotation for 5 min (100 ms on the first coil, 10 ms less on each next), while one watches dim flashes. The paper reports more right parietal EEG power in the other partner near the flash frequency: with the slowing rotation in experiment 1, this one in experiments 2 and 3.
notes: Persinger 2010, Experiment 1 (6 pairs, chairs 5 m apart): six shared rotations of 5 min each (200-20, 100-10, 20-2, 200+20, 100+10, 20+2), a 20-s EEG baseline 2 min into each, then a dim green light of about 10 lux at 8.3 Hz for 40 s; the effect was reported for 100-10, that is 100, 110, 120 ms ... (p.2 [232]). Experiment 2 (one pair, 10 m): white flashes of about 1 lux at 5, 10 and 15 Hz, EEG 30 s before and 30 s during; effect for 100+10 (p.3 [233]). Experiment 3 (3 pairs): 5, 8, 10 and 15 Hz during 100+10 or 100-10 (p.4 [234]). Both people 'received the identical complex circumcerebral magnetic field ... at any given time' (Fig. 1, p.2 [232]). This program runs 100+10 only: 100 down to 30 ms per coil, for 5 min, counter-clockwise from Fp1 to Fp2 (site names are this project's reading). The paper names neither the waveform nor the intensity ('weak, complex magnetic fields'). The Thomas pattern from the 849-point patent table at 1 ms per point, repeated back to back, and 1 uT are this project's choice, as is the flash timing in the setting. One helmet delivers one of the two exposures, so both partners run this program; two helmets started by hand have no fixed phase relation. The light source is not part of the helmet. The lab's review gives 0.5 to 1 uT for the device in general, without a place of measurement (Persinger & Lavallee 2010 p.9 [793]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Small samples, single lab, never independently replicated. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Flashing light at 5 to 15 Hz can trigger seizures in susceptible people. Do not use results for decisions about real people. Nobody with epilepsy, a seizure history or photosensitivity should take part in either role.
setting: Partner A (light): seated in a closed, quiet room with a helmet on, watching a diffuse white light of about 1 lux. Partner B (measured): another room 5 to 10 m away, second helmet running this program, EEG recorded (the outcome; the lab looked at the right parietal region). Flash trains at 5, 8, 10 and 15 Hz, 30 s each, starting at 1:00, 2:00, 3:00 and 4:00 on the program clock; take EEG for the 20 s before and the first 20 s of each train. A third person keeps the flash log away from whoever scores the EEG.
schedule: One session per pair. As a control, a helper runs both helmets on this program or on sham (the same choice for both, unknown to the partners and the scorer) on different days, and the EEG is scored blind.
source: Persinger, Saroka, Lavallee, Booth, Hunter, Mulligan, Koren, Wu & Gang 2010, Neurosci Lett 486:231-234 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20887774/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, Theoretical and experimental evidence of macroscopic entanglement between human brain activity and photon emissions, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Dotta & Persinger 2012, "Doubling" of local photon emissions when two simultaneous, spatially-separated, chemiluminescent reactions share the same magnetic field configurations, J Biophys Chem 3:72-80 (859- and 230-point patterns at 1 ms; primer/effector order) https://file.scirp.org/Html/17181.html ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University ("20-2" = 20, 22 ... 34 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008, Electromagn Biol Med 27:426-436 (counter-clockwise vs clockwise) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037792/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
